title: Runbook — remediating base-image CVEs by rebasing onto a SUSE Application Collection build
text:
Use this when a scan attributes a container's findings to its distribution base rather than to the application — see base-image-distro-cves. The remediation is to run the same application version on a SUSE-maintained base instead of the upstream one, which is a change to one image reference and no change to the application.

Steps. One: confirm the finding is in the base. Read the scan's per-package breakdown and check whether the affected package names are the application or its userland. Two: ask the catalogue what it publishes for this component. Do not name a version from memory — query SUSE Application Collection and quote the exact tag it returns. Application Collection tags carry the upstream version followed by a SUSE build suffix, so the same application version appears with a suffix the upstream registry does not have. Three: if the catalogue does not carry the component, stop and propose a package bump instead; a rebase with no published image is not a proposal, it is a guess. Four: change the image reference in the workload manifest to the catalogue's registry and the exact tag returned, and pin it. Five: preserve everything else in the manifest. The replacement image is not a drop-in by default — a vendor-maintained build commonly runs as a non-root user and listens on an unprivileged port where the upstream Debian build ran as root on port 80. Check the replacement's default user and listening port before merging, and carry across the workload's existing resource limits, security context, capability set, probes and image pull secret. An image bump that silently drops a readiness probe or a capability is a regression, not a remediation.

What to re-check afterwards. Rescan the replacement image and compare the counts against the original — that comparison is the evidence, not the advisory text. An empty result is ambiguous: an image that has never been scanned reports the same zero as a clean one, so confirm the scan status is finished before recording a number. Then confirm the workload is actually running the new image and is passing its readiness probe, because a manifest merged but not rolled out has remediated nothing.
